title: Elijah taken as into heaven, Christ truly ascended
english: riding in a chariot, not galloping in disorder across the earth but launching his course through the upper air in strikingly new glory, pressing on to round the heavenly turning post and mightily striking down the devil running beside him. But when the children of the Jews, begrudging the truth heard that Christ was taken up into the heavens, they wanted to dim the astonishing miracle of the Sun of Righteousness, so they bring in Elijah against us with these words: “Why do you Christians boast so loudly that Christ, as you say, was taken up? Elijah too was a man, counted worthy of the same glory, and he was taken up into the heavens.”

To them we answer boldly: “Why, O Jews, do you plunder the books like blind men and fail to see exactly what is written in them? Why do you read without understanding? For what does the divine Scripture say? ‘And Elijah was taken up in a whirlwind as into heaven’ (2 Kings 2:11). That ‘as into heaven’ leaves the meaning doubtful, while the bare ‘into heaven’ shows the clear truth. Neither Elijah nor anyone else has gone up into heaven, but only the only-begotten Son of God who came down from heaven, and he gives us full assurance about himself when he says, ‘No one has ascended into heaven except he who came down from heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven’ (John 3:13), the good shepherd who left the ninety-nine sheep of the angels on the heavenly mountains, found the wandering sheep, carried it on the shoulders of his love for humanity, brought it up into the heavenly harbor, and as he offers his gift to his own Father cries: ‘Father, I have found the wandering sheep, which the deceiving serpent tricked with treacherous devices, led into ways of wickedness, and stained the purity of the knowledge of God with the mud of many gods. I saw it drowning in the mire of this life and quickly snatched it up with the right hand of my divinity. With tender mercy I washed it in the streams of the Jordan and anointed it with the fragrance of my Holy Spirit, and now through the resurrection I have come, bringing to you a worthy gift for your Godhead, the sheep endowed with reason.’”

Today the devil mourns his own defeat as he watches our body carried up into the heavens. Today sin is scattered like smoke by the ascension of Christ Jesus. Today the devil wails and says: “What shall I do in my misery? Like a keen-swooping hawk he snatched from me all the people of every age, left me desolate, clipped my wings on every side, and dashed me to the ground.”
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Homilia in assumptionem Christi u01-rem-early
orientation: The preacher finishes his chariot image of Christ in flesh going to heaven, then answers Jewish objectors who cite Elijah, then gives Christ as shepherd presenting the found sheep to the Father as the devil starts to lament.

title: The devil confesses he was tricked and beaten
english: The devil goes on in his lament: “The Son of Mary deceived me. I did not know that God was hidden in a human body. I saw him wrapped in a human body, and I took him for a mere human and stirred the Jews against him. What I did not dare to do by myself, I worked through the Jews. I contrived myriads of false accusations. I devised every kind of insult against him. With a reed I gave him drink, and with a sponge I gave him drink. I crowned his head with thorns. I shamed him with slaps. I nailed him to the cross with nails. In the end I handed him over to death, and as if I had won, I celebrated with the Jews.”

He continues: “When I saw him risen on the third day, as I had said before, I collapsed as if a sword had suddenly pierced my heart. When I saw him eating and drinking, I was preparing another cross for him. But while I was turning this over in my mind, I see him going up in glory into heaven, from which I fell in disgrace.” Therefore the psalmist also cried out long ago, saying, “All you nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of gladness, for the Lord is the Most High, a fearful king, great over all the earth” (Psalm 47:1-2), and again, “God has ascended with a shout, the Lord with the sound of the trumpet” (Psalm 47:5).

Then the devil says again: “I want to chase after him, but I sink like lead. I want to seize him, but I am thrust off invisibly. What am I to do in my misery? From every side he has encircled me. From heaven he slung me down to earth like a tiny stone. When I fell to the earth, I wanted to hide in the waters. He found me hiding in the streams of the Jordan like a dragon, seized me, and scourged me. If I try even to hold on to the earth, all its keepers, like guardians of a master’s flock, shout the cry against me, ‘The earth is the Lord’s and all that fills it, the world and all who live in it’ (Psalm 24:1).”

The earthquake proved that the earth is the Lord’s. The earth could not bear the Lord’s name and shook with uncontrollable trembling. It was scourged for the disorder of its children. It opened up cracks against the elements like a mouth and cried out the greatness of its hidden pain. Like a mother for her children, it begged him to spare those who had sinned.

“Who will tell of the mighty acts of the Lord? Who will make all his praises heard?” (Psalm 106:2) The earth is the Lord’s and all that fills it. For Christ united to himself the flesh formed from the earth, and he sat down in the heavens. Now the devil comes, wanting to defile it through sexual sin.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Homilia in assumptionem Christi u01-rem-mid
orientation: The devil continues his first person lament telling how he drove the Jews to kill Christ and how Christ still rose and went up.

title: The good soil bears fruit and he will come again in the body
english: But keep watch like a guard with a sleepless eye for your soul. Do not allow the robber to break through the eye of your mind, so that you can say to him with boldness, “I am no betrayer of my Master’s property, devil. For the earth is the Lord’s (Psalm 24:1), and so is Christ’s Church, tilled at all times by the rain from heaven and bearing fresh fruit for Christ thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.”

“A sower went out to sow,” Scripture says (Matthew 13:3). Some seed fell on the road, which is Greek deception. Then the birds came, the ravenous demon plunderers, and devoured it. Other seed fell on rocky ground, which, I mean, is the hard-hearted resolve of the Jews, and at once a growth of recklessness and lawlessness shot up. Such, indeed, is the way of the Jews. For while they were receiving the law in the desert, they said to Moses, “All that God has said, we will do and we will hear” (Exodus 24:7). Yet the very men who promised this worshiped a lifeless calf and set a dead thing above the living God.

Other seed fell among thorns, which are the rough-spined and foul-mouthed heresies that choke the seed of piety day after day. But other seed fell on the good soil, which is Christ’s fruitful Church, bearing fruit thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold. Thirtyfold is the yoke of self-control, sixtyfold is angel-like virginity, and a hundredfold is divine righteousness and purity and the brave deeds of the martyrs.

The heralds of piety proclaimed the Lord’s coming at the end to all, saying, “He will come in the same way you saw him ascending” (Acts 1:11). For two men appeared in white clothing (Acts 1:10). Two, so that the truth would be believed; men, to strengthen the disciples into manliness; in white, to flood the minds of their hearers with light. What, then, did those who appeared proclaim? “Men of Israel, why do you stand looking into heaven? Why do you gaze into the sky? Look instead on the Maker of heaven, glorify the greatness of him who is ascending, and marvel at his coming down in love for humanity. For he united the earthly man to himself and made him a citizen of heaven and a dweller in heaven. O wonder, where he has lifted up the one who lay below!”

Why do you stand looking into heaven? He will come in this way. In what way? He will come wearing our body and holding before him the side wounded by the spear, so that the Jews will see him whom they pierced (John 19:37). And may we be counted worthy to see his face with boldness and to obtain the promised goods, by the grace and love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ, with whom be glory, might, and honor to the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Homilia in assumptionem Christi u01-rem-close
orientation: Epiphanius the preacher is closing the homily by applying the parable of the sower to the Church and repeating what the two men in white announced about Christ's return.
